(a) The top view (perpendicular to the benzoquinone plane) of both π-dimers HOMOs is quite similar to that of the SOMO of the anion-radicals. As such, the in-plane electron distributions within π-bonded moieties are similar to that of the monomeric anion-radical, in accord with the invariance of the corresponding bond-lengths within anionic moieties of monomeric, dimeric, separated or ion-paired p-benzoquinones (Table S1 in the ESI).

(b) The single-point Gaussian 98 calculations (based on the X-ray orthogonal coordinates of the [DDQ2]2−π-dimers) reveal that in the absence of the counter-ions, the π-dimer with the longitudial offset is more stable than that with the transversal offset (Table S2 in the ESI). However, the energy of sodium-tethered dimer is lower than the energy of the separated dimer (calculated, for consistency, with the two distant sodium cations)
